newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM hedges 60 pct of 1997/98 fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: KLM hedges 60 pct of 1997/98 fuel costs.

text.p: Dutch carrier KLM said on Tuesday it had covered 60 percent of its exposure to fuel cost fluctuations for 1997/98 at around current prices.
"We are very busy with hedging policy...60 percent of aviation fuel needs have been hedged for 1997/98," outgoing KLM president Pieter Bouw told the annual shareholders' meeting.
The hedging was at a level "about the current low prices," he said, adding an unexpected jump in fuel prices had contributed to the poor operating earnings of 1996/97.
KLM said earlier aircraft fuel costs had been a major factor behind an 11 percent rise in first-quarter unit costs.
The airline on Tuesday reported 1997/98 first-quarter operating profits up 164 million guilders at 244 million.
Last year, KLM's operating result plunged to a 201 million guilder loss after provisions for restructuring.
"Fuel costs (in 1996/97) were 170 million guilders more than budgeted, even when taking into account that the price risk was hedged for 55 million guilders," Bouw said.
